builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Inference Validation for Regulated AI: Building a Decision Pipeline on NVIDIA AIPerf
summary: The technique replaces ad hoc or engine-default inference benchmarking with a governed validation harness that wraps NVIDIA AIPerf: AIPerf supplies the measurement, while Runway adds experiment design, caching-as-audit storage, and compliance/cost decision logic. The cost is non-trivial engineering effort to build and maintain the harness, storage for audit artifacts, and compute budget for sweeps across engines, GPU instance types, and concurrency levels. What can fail: rankings between engines (TensorRT-LLM vs vLLM) invert with concurrency and speculative decoding behaves differently across engines under load, so conclusions drawn at one operating point may mislead at production load, and the harness itself must be trusted to remain correct as engines and hardware evolve.
rationale: The reader has constrained infrastructure and needs to pick an inference engine and GPU instance for production; the paper's core finding (that rankings invert with concurrency and configuration can outweigh engine choice) means adopting the validation practice is worthwhile, but the reader must validate against their own workload before trusting any specific engine or hardware conclusion.
technique: Governed inference validation pipeline around NVIDIA AIPerf
